dedupe_keys.name: aliso canyon gas storage well failure 2015 to 2016 leak and cpuc investigation and reliability assessments

description: This case study follows the Aliso Canyon Natural Gas Storage Facility, the largest gas storage facility in California in the Santa Susana Mountains, from the well failure discovered by SoCalGas crews on 23 October 2015 to the California Public Utilities Commission's continuing investigation and reliability assessments. The leak was stopped on 12 February 2016, the well sealed three days later and later plugged and abandoned; after inspection of all wells the CPUC and CalGEM found the facility safe and it reopened on 19 July 2017 at reduced capacity, with a maximum allowable pressure of 2,926 psi and an inventory of 68.6 Bcf against a pre-leak capacity of 86 Bcf. The page lists the 2017 Order Instituting Investigation, the August 2023 settlement decision, the removal of the withdrawal protocol, summer and winter reliability assessments since 2016 with CAISO, CEC and LADWP, and a first biennial assessment in October 2025. Access: pages, decisions and assessments on the CPUC site, free; no licence is stated. Caveats: a regulator's narrative with links, not a dataset. It suits gas-electric interdependency, storage capacity planning and resilience policy studies, and relates to the San Bruno pipeline rupture case study catalogued here.
